title: Shipping booking replay and recovery are governed by the journal, not mutable method settings
question: Should changing or archiving a shipping method block replay or recovery of an already journaled carrier operation?

options.text: Journal first: validate current method only for a new operation or a fresh attempt after rejected; booked returns its durable result without resolving a carrier, recovery uses the original immutable payload and original carrier contribution
options.pros: Method maintenance cannot strand a shipment; conflicts, lease and fencing stay authoritative

options.text: Validate current method on every call before reading the journal
options.cons: Archive/carrier changes deny replay and prevent find for possibly existing shipments

context: P6 audit A2: carrier() checked the current method before claim(), so an archived method or changed carrier stranded unknown bookings and denied durable booked replays. D29 promises stored-result replay and recovery by the original reference and fingerprint.
decision: A — Journal first: validate current method only for a new operation or a fresh attempt after rejected; booked returns its durable result without resolving a carrier, recovery uses the original immutable payload and original carrier contribution
rationale: Owner delegated architecture and explicitly authorized audit corrections. Journal authority preserves D29 for already accepted operations; new/rejected attempts still validate the current method. No public signature or schema change; unavailable original carrier fails closed and leaves recovery retryable.
